title: Phaistos disc
caveat: These are questions about the material that can be measured before anyone proposes a reading. Answering all of them would not decipher the script; it would make a later claim testable. Nothing here is a reading, and no probability of decipherment is assigned.

lay.tagline: A clay disc from Bronze Age Crete stamped with signs found nowhere else.
lay.summary: The Phaistos disc is a clay disc about 16 centimetres across, found in 1908 in the palace of Phaistos on Crete. Its 241 signs were pressed in with stamps, in a spiral, on both sides, and grouped into 61 sections. No other text uses the same signs, which makes any reading almost impossible to test. We have not proposed one. The plan is to reconcile the published sign lists first and measure how much any result depends on the disputed signs.
lay.what_it_is: There are 45 distinct signs. Because there is only one object, a reading invented from the disc cannot be checked against a second text.
lay.what_we_found: Nothing has been executed for the Phaistos disc in this project yet.
lay.whats_next: Compare two independent sign transcriptions, freeze a small number of grouping variants, and report how much each disputed sign changes the statistics.

faq.q: Has the Phaistos disc been deciphered?
faq.a: No. Many readings have been proposed; with a single short text none can be confirmed.
That has been argued, but the Heraklion Museum treats it as genuine and the question is not settled here.

researcher.summary: Heraklion Archaeological Museum description: 241 stamped signs in 61 groups on two sides, read from the edge inward. Planned: reconcile two cited annotations against the museum count, freeze at most 12 grouping variants, and compare repeated-group and sign-position statistics with at most 2,000 within-side permutations per statistic.

statuses.closed-with-power: Answered with a control: measured on a frozen corpus, with a solved or synthetic control showing the method works.
statuses.tested-without-power: Measured without a control: a number exists, but no control shows what it would look like if the answer were different.
statuses.open: Open: proposed here, not yet measured.

families.family: Do the published sign lists agree with the museum's 241 signs?
families.next: Reconcile two independent annotations location by location against the museum count and keep every discrepancy.

families.family: How much do repeated-group statistics depend on disputed signs and boundaries?
